taskDescription: Drag the correct pattern name into each blank.
textField: When ALT and AST are raised many times the upper limit with only a modest ALP rise, the pattern is *hepatocellular*; when ALP and GGT are disproportionately raised with conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, the pattern is *cholestatic*; and when increased red-cell breakdown raises unconjugated bilirubin, with absent urine bilirubin and increased urine urobilinogen, the pattern is *haemolytic*.

overallFeedback.feedback: Hepatocellular injury releases ALT and AST from dying hepatocytes; cholestasis (the biochemical pattern) induces ALP synthesis and traps conjugated bilirubin — imaging then distinguishes extrahepatic obstruction from intrahepatic cholestasis; haemolysis overwhelms conjugation capacity, raising unconjugated bilirubin without affecting liver enzymes. Isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with normal enzymes can also reflect impaired conjugation, as in Gilbert syndrome or Crigler-Najjar syndrome, not only haemolysis. Recognising the pattern directs imaging and further testing.
